goal: Choose Nix build limits from measured build time and interactive terminal latency, preserving evidence so future changes do not repeat unsupported reversals.

decision.action: Retain the existing Nix settings; no configuration change.
decision.reason: The existing setting passed all three trials. Both higher-parallelism candidates failed the predeclared terminal latency bound in two of three trials.
decision.interpretation: This supports retaining the existing cap under the observed live-system conditions. Varying background work prevents an isolated causal claim about the latency differences or a claim that this setting is globally optimal.
decision.required_follow_up: None for this experiment. A future proposal to change these limits needs new comparable measurements that pass the stated bounds.

measurement_scope: Kira, Apple M5, 10 cores, 24 GiB RAM; one clean Herdr release compilation after 48 small instruction artifacts, with cached dependencies and the existing desktop session running.
limitations: The terminal probe measures command dispatch through the running Herdr server until output appears in its buffer, including CLI and 20 ms polling overhead. It does not measure physical input or graphical repaint latency.
The workload contains only one large compilation at a time. It does not establish safe concurrency for several large derivations or reproduce the original overlapping evaluators.
Normal user services continue running. Counterbalanced repetitions reduce order bias but do not eliminate background workload or thermal effects.
Measurements apply to Kira. Rin and Linux hosts were not benchmarked.
Nix cores controls builder parallelism where supported; it is not a hard operating-system CPU limit.
The experiment measures build execution, not the cost of overlapping Nix evaluators or MCP sessions.
history_interpretation: Linux commits contain conflicting rationales, not comparable benchmarks. A full patch-history search in this repository found no earlier macOS max-jobs or cores limit.

observed_background_activity.round_1_previous: A separate browser recording session began during this trial.
observed_background_activity.round_2_previous: A concurrent browser recording and ffmpeg encode overlapped this trial. A live snapshot measured ffmpeg at 498.1 percent CPU, roughly five logical cores. The trial failed the terminal p95 bound, but the overlap prevents attributing that failure to the core setting alone.
observed_background_activity.round_2_current: The encoder was no longer running by the sample taken approximately one minute into this trial; remaining browser and desktop services were not stopped.
observed_background_activity.round_2_intermediate: Separate browser recording continued. A live snapshot showed browser renderers and recording activity; no claim isolates the latency failure to the Nix core setting.
observed_background_activity.round_3_intermediate: The same live desktop remained active; this trial also encountered elevated terminal latency.
observed_background_activity.round_3_previous: The live desktop remained active. This trial failed the terminal latency bound; background activity was not held constant across candidates.

machine.runtime_verification: Herdr 0.9.1 server PID 36927 started before the warmup and all measured trials and remained running afterward. The benchmark used the same 0.9.0 CLI throughout and never restarted or activated the shared server.

notes: Terminal command-to-buffer roundtrip, not GUI paint latency.
Dependencies and filesystem caches are warm; each target is rebuilt in a fresh Nix build directory.
Warmup excluded; three repeats in a counterbalanced order.
Scored builds use standard overrideAttrs with a unique unused benchmarkIteration attribute. Installed package is never replaced.
protocol.selection_rule: Qualify only candidates with all 3 trials successful, terminal p95 <= 100 ms in every trial, normal memory pressure, <= 64 MiB swapout growth per trial, and no timeouts. Change from current only if median build time improves >= 10 percent, or current fails these bounds. Otherwise retain current; do not claim a global optimum.
protocol.workload_order: Rebuild the same 48 instruction artifacts, then compile the same Herdr source into a fresh per-trial output; dependencies are cached.
protocol.excluded_warmup: The warmup compiled Herdr successfully in 380.23 seconds. Nix rejected the output comparison because the rebuilt output differed from the installed output. That run is excluded from all scored results.
protocol.isolated_output_verification: All nine derivations were compared with the original installed derivation. Only benchmarkIteration and output paths differed; source, flags, toolchain and dependencies were identical.

terminal_probe.read: herdr pane read PANE_ID --source recent --lines 8 --format text
terminal_probe.success: The unique marker appears as a complete standalone line.
terminal_probe.latency: Monotonic elapsed time from CLI dispatch until the marker is read, including subprocess startup and polling overhead.
terminal_probe.percentile: Nearest rank: sorted samples at index ceil(sample_count * 0.95) - 1.

build_commands: nix build --no-link --json --max-jobs JOBS --cores CORES --rebuild ARTIFACT_DRV_1^* ... ARTIFACT_DRV_48^*
protocol.sampling: iostat -w 1 for whole-machine CPU, excluding its initial lifetime-average sample; vm_stat and kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level every 2 seconds for memory and swap counters.
protocol.abort_conditions: Three consecutive terminal timeouts, two consecutive non-normal memory-pressure samples, or 15 minutes per trial. None occurred.
protocol.build_duration: Elapsed wall time around both sequential build commands, including process polling and sampler shutdown. Derivation instantiation happens before timing.
